office_does: A State Representative writes and votes on Washington state law and the operating, capital and transportation budgets, covering school funding, tax structure, housing rules, health funding and criminal-justice statutes.
race_blurb: Democratic incumbent Julio Cortes, seeking a third term, faces Army veteran and nurse Jeff Kelly of the centrist Cascade Party after a primary in which Cortes took about half the vote. Both put affordability first; they differ on the 2026 millionaires tax, rent limits and how to approach public safety.

candidates.summary: Two-term incumbent and City of Everett economic-development manager whose record includes votes for the millionaires tax, rent-increase limits and juvenile diversion standards.
highlights: Voted for ESSB 6346, the 2026 tax on income over $1 million, and co-signed a session report celebrating it [S6][S7]
Co-sponsored and voted for the 2025 limit on annual rent increases, while also backing faster permitting [S9][S10][S11]
Cites standardizing juvenile diversion programs and wants more funding for diversion and reentry support [S1][S11]

taxes.basis: Voted for the 9.9% tax on income over $1 million, co-signed a report calling it historic, promoted it in interviews and would consider lifting the 1% property-tax growth cap.

spending.basis: Defends programs such as early learning and child care but says the state should not fund programs it cannot sustain and should cut low-impact ones: genuinely mixed.

housing.basis: Co-sponsored and voted for the 2025 rent-increase cap, while also calling for cutting red tape and faster permitting to add supply.

safety.basis: Cites standardizing juvenile diversion and wants to shift money from jailing youth and adults to support systems and social-worker programs; also wants police hiring that reflects communities.

climate.basis: Said the state should be more aggressive at targeting major polluters and investing in green technology; single interview statement.

healthcare.basis: Reported by the Herald as among sponsors of a 2025 Washington Health Trust (universal coverage) bill that died in committee; no statement of his own on single-payer.

immigration.basis: Co-signed a session report expressing concern about ICE actions and listing passed bills restricting masked officers and immigration enforcement's use of license plate readers.

experience.basis: Incumbent since 2022 seeking a third term, against a first-time candidate; a shorter tenure than a senior legislator.

social.basis: Pamphlet pledges to keep fighting for reproductive rights and lists a Planned Parenthood endorsement; no LGBTQ+ or sports statement.

parental-rights.basis: Voted for ESHB 1296, which modified the I-2081 parental-rights list; no campaign statement on the topic.

candidates.summary: First-time Cascade Party candidate, an Army combat medic, registered nurse and north Everett neighborhood chair, running on affordability, law-enforcement funding and spending review.
highlights: Would 'fully fund law enforcement' and treat addiction without 'enabling' it [S1][S2]
Wants lower taxes and a smaller state gas tax, and a fairer 'proportional' tax plan [S1][S2][S4]
Would run cost-benefit reviews of state programs and expects spending cuts [S4]
Favors builder-friendly housing policy and faster permits [S2][S4]

taxes.basis: Lists lowering taxes and a gas-tax cut as priorities, but also calls the system regressive and promises an undefined fairer plan, so not maximal.

spending.basis: Says the Legislature must cut spending and would run cost-benefit analysis of programs, while warning against cavalier cuts.

housing.basis: Would increase housing through builder-friendly policies and streamlined permits; no tenant-protection position.

safety.basis: Would fully fund law enforcement and retail-theft units and treat addiction 'not enable it', while also funding behavioral health services.

climate.basis: Calls for reducing the state gas tax burden at the pump; no position on carbon pricing or clean energy.

experience.basis: First-time candidate with no elected office, from a new third party, running on outsider 'accountability'.
